context.title: Context budget
context.layers: Counted: the always-loaded files of the target that the scan reads. Not counted: the user memory, the memory of the parent folders (listed by the scan, not measured), the auto memory, and the memory of subfolders, which loads when Claude works in its folder.
context.layersAncestors: Counted: the always-loaded files of the target that the scan reads. Not counted: the user memory, the memory of the parent folders (read by the scan, but not counted in the total), the auto memory, and the memory of subfolders, which loads when Claude works in its folder.
context.agents: AGENTS.md: the scan assumes that Claude Code reads AGENTS.md only when no CLAUDE.md or CLAUDE.local.md exists in the target or in a parent folder, which is the default. Only the user or managed settings can change that, so project settings cannot. If the assumption is wrong, the table misses that file.
context.byLayerNote: On demand is what Claude Code loads when it works in the layer: the CLAUDE.md files of the folders on the way to the layer and inside it, and the rules whose paths match a file of the layer; nested skills and nested AGENTS.md are not verified, so the skills are shown but not added to the total, and the AGENTS.md files are not counted.
context.unknownTitle: Not estimated: these items enter the context, but their size cannot be known without running them.
unknown.hook-output: hook {event} with matcher {matcher}, declared in {source}; its output enters the context

limits.title: Limits of this scan
limits.notRead: Not read: the user layer (memory and settings in the user's Claude folder), the parent folders of the target, and the files that the scan skipped, listed below.
limits.readBoth: Read: the user layer (memory, settings, rules, skills and subagents in the user's Claude folder, ~/.claude) and the instruction files of the parent folders of the target. Not read: the files that the scan skipped, listed below.
limits.readUser: Read: the user layer (memory, settings, rules, skills and subagents in the user's Claude folder, ~/.claude). Not read: the parent folders of the target, and the files that the scan skipped, listed below.
limits.readAncestors: Read: the instruction files of the parent folders of the target. Not read: the user layer (memory and settings in the user's Claude folder, ~/.claude), and the files that the scan skipped, listed below.
limits.scope: The scan was limited to a scope: the folder tree, the map coverage, the large and generated files, and the duplication were measured only inside the scope folders. Read outside the scope: the harness of every agent at the root and in the inherited folders, the project permissions and hooks, the secret files of the whole target, the root package.json, the tool configs, the CI workflows, and the package.json files of `verification.packages`. Apart from those files, the {outside} files outside the scope were not analyzed, and neither was the harness of the folders that lie neither inside the scope nor between the root and the scope.
limits.estimate: Tokens are estimated, never counted. Method: {method}.
limits.thresholds: The thresholds are {status}: each value is an assumption that calibration has not confirmed.
limits.thresholdsCalibrated: The thresholds are {status}: each value was confirmed or changed on the evidence of a calibration document.
limits.thresholdsMixed: Some thresholds are calibrated and others are provisional: each threshold shows its own status where it is cited.
limits.sec02: The SEC-02 triggers assume the project's `defaultMode`, or `default` when the project sets none. The scan used {mode}. A session may start in another mode (not verified against the documentation). The matrix shows each mode.
limits.matrix: Outcome of each destructive command for a session started in each mode. It is context, not a trigger: the SEC-02 findings do not use it.
limits.matrixLegend: `auto` = decided by a model classifier, not simulated; rules deciding before the mode is not verified for `auto` and `bypassPermissions` (only deny is stated to apply in every mode); hooks are not used; `dontAsk` and `plan` are not shown.
limits.matrixLocations: Locations: inside the project; outside the project; critical path, such as the home folder or the root. The standard depth shows each command only at its own location.
limits.undeterminable: Cases that the rules could not decide. They are not findings:

remediation.title: Remediation
remediation.intro: Nothing here is written to the target and nothing is applied for you. Each fragment is a settings object: review it, then copy its lists by hand into the permissions of your project settings, if you agree with it.
remediation.summary: {fragments} fragments: {simulated} simulated, {notSimulated} not simulated. Destructive commands that pass today: {passing}. In the simulation with the patch applied: {moved} move off passing (not verified in auto and bypassPermissions), {stillPassing} still pass, {unsimulated} are not simulated.
remediation.omitted: Left out, because each list holds at most {cap} items: {fragments} fragments, {commands} commands, {reads} secret reads and {notSimulated} literal secrets. The counts above are for the items kept in this file.
remediation.fragments.title: Fragments
remediation.fragments.none: No fragment: no measured finding needs one, and no agent fragment was given.
remediation.rule.SEC-02: Ask before a destructive command runs
remediation.rule.SEC-03: Deny the Read tool on a secret file
remediation.field.settings: Settings to copy by hand, after review:
remediation.text.sec01: A broad shell allow lets these destructive commands through. The allow stays; the rules below make these commands ask first, or block them when the data marks them critical. In auto and bypassPermissions that ask is not verified.
remediation.text.sec02: This command passes in the scan, by a rule or in a permission mode of its matrix. The rule below makes it ask before it runs, or block it when the data marks it critical. It covers the sample command and the same prefix followed by any arguments. It does not cover a reordered or respelled form, such as git push origin --force for git push --force. The ask is not verified in auto and bypassPermissions: only deny is stated to apply in every mode.
remediation.text.sec03: The Read tool cannot open this file with the rule below. The deny also blocks Edit and Write on it. It does not remove the file from version control, and it does not stop a command that reads the file without naming it.
remediation.reason.simulation-mismatch: the simulated value before the patch differs from the measured one, so this is not simulated
remediation.reason.unsupported-path: the path has characters that a rule may read as a pattern; write the rule by hand
remediation.reason.not-permission: not a permission rule: a hook or a text change, which is not simulated
remediation.reason.not-modelled-rule: a rule of a kind this simulation does not model (only Bash, PowerShell and Read rules are simulated)
remediation.reason.no-matrix: the scan has no permission matrix for this command
remediation.reason.not-in-data: the command is not in the data file of this version of the tool
remediation.reason.undecidable-rule: a rule that the simulation cannot decide for every path or command (for example a home path, ~/, or a parameter rule): the fragment is not applied
remediation.reason.no-rule: the fragment has no deny or ask rule, so there is nothing to simulate
remediation.reason.literal-secret: a literal secret is a value inside a file, not a permission: move the value out of the file, and rotate it if the file was ever versioned
remediation.commands.title: Destructive commands, before and after
remediation.commands.legend: Each cell shows the outcome before the patch, then after it (before → after), for the measured mode and for each mode of the matrix. Results: moved (it passed and now asks or blocks), classifier (no mode passes it, and auto mode would leave the decision to a model: not a move), still passes, undeterminable, unchanged (it did not pass before), not simulated. The modes marked not verified, auto and bypassPermissions, have outcomes that are not verified against the documentation.
remediation.result.classifier: classifier (auto mode would leave it to a model: not a move)
remediation.reads.title: Secret files, before and after
remediation.reads.legend: The decision of a Read of each secret file, measured and after the patch. deny blocks the read; default, allow and ask let it through (ask with a prompt).
remediation.notSimulated.title: Not simulated
remediation.literal: {file}, line {line}: a {kind} value written in the file ({reason}).
remediation.hooks: Hooks are not simulated: a hook runs code, and this tool runs no code from the target. Read each hook's matcher, script and onFailure yourself.
remediation.limits.title: What this does not cover
remediation.limit.apply: Nothing is applied. The person copies each fragment by hand, after review; the tool never writes to the target.
remediation.limit.hooks: Hooks are out of scope of this remediation, and no fragment is a hook.
remediation.limit.read: A Read deny covers the Read tool, Edit and Write on the same path, and the file commands that Claude Code recognizes in Bash, such as cat. It does not cover a command that reads a file without naming it, or a script that opens a file itself.
remediation.limit.modes: Auto mode is decided by a classifier, which this simulation does not run, so its outcome is classifier and not a verdict. Only deny is stated to apply in every mode. The ask and allow outcomes of auto and bypassPermissions, and the outcomes that bypassPermissions gives without a rule, are not verified against the documentation: the tables mark them as not verified.
remediation.limit.userLayer: The user settings are not in the permissions that the scan records. A command whose simulated before differs from the measured value is marked not simulated, and its fragment is not applied to the simulation.
